calls.head: Power against power
calls.body: At home, the Flyers keep sending Zegras’s line (Dvorak, Zegras and Foerster) out against opponents’ first lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Rick Tocchet has been choosing strength on strength. Tonight the Avalanche’s first line is Lehkonen, MacKinnon and Nečas.

surprises.head: Both teams played to type
surprises.body: Nothing in this game strayed far from how these two usually play: the shot share, the quality of chances, special teams, hitting, ice time and goaltending all landed inside their normal night-to-night range.

story.head: The Flyers squeak past the Avalanche
paras: Matvei Michkov got the scoring started for the Flyers on the power play midway through the first, and the goal stood after the Avalanche challenged for goalie interference. Michkov scored his second of the night midway through the second to make it 2-0, but Martin Nečas got the Avs on the board late in the period. Noel Acciari scored his first goal for Philadelphia early in the third to make it 3-1 for the Flyers, and that one stood up as the winner. T.J. Hughes pulled the Avalanche within one late in the period. Trevor Zegras finished with three assists.
The Flyers had a bit more of the good stuff. Joseph Woll made 24 saves for the Flyers, and Mackenzie Blackwood stopped 21 of 24.
The Avalanche hit two posts and still lost. The Flyers improved to 2-6-3, and the Avalanche dropped to 5-3-1.
